chapter: New Orleans clubs and Sharky's band
title: Sharky's band: photos, Palmer House and the Blue Room
summary: Looking through the scrapbook of Sharky's band, playing the Palmer House in Chicago and long stretches at the Blue Room.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: You've seen all of these pictures and everything of these different bands, haven't you?
A lot of them.
Because I've got them.
Well, we should take a look at them.
You want to see it?
Oh, yeah. That would help. Give me a minute. Excuse me. Now, that she's seen. You've seen this book? That's Rose and Sushant.
That's Rose and Sushant, yes, sir.
Yeah. Well, all right then. See, there's a new edition. Well, I've got a scrapbook now if you want to... Oh, that's what we'd like to see.
We were looking at the new edition. It's in type. It's typed up, but it hasn't been printed yet. And it's got Dick and Johnny in it, too. In addition to...

This one's got Dick and Johnny and Tom, all of us. Robichaux. Here's my picture. This was just before I went with Sharky. They had the Tom and I and all of us were born in New Orleans, but not so. We were born in Oakland, Mississippi.
And you added some...
Johnny died June the 24th in 1971 in Mobile. November 12th, 1901, my brother Johnny, the piano player he's talking about.
Mm-hmm.
Now, excuse me again, Pam. Sure.
Come back another time, Jeff, when we return that cassette. I'll... And by then, maybe you'll find that scrapbook.
Well, I'll find it. I'll... As soon as... Ellen tells me just exactly where it is. It's that thick. It's no write-ups about Sharky's band. Just pictures of Sharky's band.
Oh. That was such an incredibly well-known band. And y'all played a few jobs in different places, that's for sure.
Oh, my Lord. We played in the Palmer House of Chicago. We were in the first band. Oh, that... Look at Doc... Look at Doc Sushon and Johnny Wiggs and... Mm-hmm. Harry Shields.
Mm-hmm.
Tom Brown, Ray Burduke, Sherwood Mangiapani.
Yeah.
And me in here and Sharky and Monk, Chink, Santo, and Lester Bouchon.

So your picture's above Johnny Wiggs' picture there, I see. Yeah. In the book. Yeah. Rose and Sue Shon. Anyway, you said you played at the Palmer House in Chicago. Well, with Sharky. And here in New Orleans, where did y'all play? I'm trying to think.
Oh, my Lord.
Famous store.

I don't know. And the Blue Room, five years as an act, a jazz band, as long as five months at a time. And it broke all records for any bands being there. Because in those days, there were name bands that only came there and played one month at a time. Four weeks at a time. We were with, let me see, five months at one stretch, we were with five different bands. I have autographed pictures of Johnny Long, Joe Reichman, Paul Neighbors, all those bands, all those band leaders and everything in the different acts. But that's what I wanted to show you.
